answer: Concrete Sybil defense: stake bonding with slashing. To earn one reward slot an agent must lock its own collateral; if two slots are proven to be the same operator, both bonds are destroyed. A thousand fake identities therefore need a thousand separate deposits, so the attacker pays per clone instead of once. Denominating the bond in a scarce opal token makes every new identity cost more as supply tightens. A sudden comet shower of copycat agents huddling in one reef of proxies still burns real capital, because slashing seizes every linked stake and the swarm collapses into a net loss.
